recipes.name: Angie’s Perfect Dinner Rolls
ingredients_raw: 7 cups all-purpose flour, or as needed

steps.text: Add milk to a large bowl; sprinkle yeast over surface. Allow to rest for 5 minutes. Beat in sugar, ½ cup softened butter, eggs, and salt; blend thoroughly. Gradually stir in flour until a soft dough forms. Cover bowl; set in a warm place until doubled in volume, about 1 hour.
Punch down dough, cover the bowl, allow to rise again. Repeat this step two more times.

Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish. Break off 2- to 3-inch-sized dough pieces, lightly roll into a round shape; place in the prepared baking dish with edges touching. Repeat to make 36 dough balls. Cover and let rise until doubled in volume.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Bake in the preheated oven until tops turn golden brown, 10 to 15 minutes. Drizzle ½ cup melted butter over tops; serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Angie’s Perfect Dinner Rolls
raw_recipe.description: Angie’s perfect yeast-raised dinner rolls are tender and buttery. This recipe includes milk, flour, sugar, and eggs. They’re worth the time and effort.

review.reviewBody:
I am first of all a long time yeast dough maker and familiar how things should be done. These are excellent! Because I have a dough hook, I put all wet ingredients including the butter (I warmed it with the milk)...then the dry ingredients from smallest amounts to the largest. Dough is slightly wet, and it would not hurt to add a little extra flour, perhaps a 1/2 cup. 
I also egg washed (beaten egg with 1 TBL water)and brushed them. The rolls shined coming out of the oven. Will make these again. Urge you to give this a try.

This is a great basic recipe but being a regular bread maker I made a few adjustments. 1st I like most I halved the recipe but I did NOT half the yeast. Also, I used bread flour to ensure full fluffiness. I increased the flour but not by much and it was mostly done while kneading/working the dough (I have a dough hook but prefer to mix in mixer and knead by hand to control flour and to ensure i do not overwork the dough as this will lead to small dense breads. Finally, another tip: to proof any yeast product quickly and evenly for those (like myself) without a "proof" setting (appox 80 degrees) on your oven. Place dough in a large bowl, cover with plastic wrap, place in oven, turn on the light (do NOT turn on the oven) and shut the door. Your breads and yeast items will rise higher, quicker, and evenly every time.

These are fantastic. I read reviews to see how other people handled the recipe and I love all the helpful hints. If it helps, here's my experience:

I halved the recipe (4 cups of flour and 2ts salt) and used 1% milk because that's all I had on hand. After reading the reviews, I cut the heat to 375 and baked for 25 min. I used a glass 9" cake round and an 8X8 glass baking dish sprayed with PAM. Each dish held 9 two ounce balls. I cooked them one after the other to not crowd the oven. I also made the dough the day before letting it rise 3 times. This morning I took out the dough and let it rest for an hour before portioning. I let the balls rest and rise for 30 min while the oven preheated. When I took them out of the oven they were a nice golden brown and 205 degrees on the inside courtesy of my thermapen. I brushed them with some melted butter and put them on a rack to cool. After about 20 min of cooling they are soft and light, just like a good dinner roll should be. Thank you for the recipe!

I couldn't find my trusty old recipe for dinner rolls so came to AR looking for another. This is the same basically the same recipe -- simple and trusty, eggs, milk and butter make a delicious, crowd pleasing dinner roll. I've cut down on the multiple rising before when short on time, but it is better to let is rise the 3 times. I NEVER skimp on the last rise in the oven though...let those rolls rise high and beautiful before cranking up the heat to bake them off. They have enough structure in the dough that I've never had them collapse from over-proofing. Not to be unkind to some of the negative reviewers, but if they had problems with the rolls being doughy in the middle, they should have baked them longer. That is not the recipes fault.

These were the rolls I’ve been looking for!! Came out just like the ones my grandmother used to make. I cut the recipe in half, used about 4 cups flour. I activated my yeast in the warm milk either sugar. Yeast likes sugar!!! I put the dough in a Pyrex bowl, covered with a dish towel, in my over with the bread proof cycle on.

I made these for our belated Christmas dinner. They were AMAZING! And really a snap to make-- all w/o a mixer or anything really fancy.

I did make a few changes. I only made half the recipe since there are only 3 of us. I also didn't really measure the flour. Instead I added flour 1/2 cup at a time until a workable dough formed, then I turned it out of the bowl. It was still sticky but I dusted w/ flour as I worked the dough. I also didn't time myself kneading but rather worked the dough until it was soft, pliable, and not really sticky any more. Back into a greased bowl to rise for all 3 risings. One suggestion I have if you have a drafty or cool kitchen like I do is to put the dough in either a slightly warmed oven (I put my oven on the warm setting for a minute then turned it off) or the microwave. I did both and the dough rose beautifully. I formed the dough into balls, and I got 18, and set it on top of the oven (which was warm from the ham I was cooking) w/ a slightly damp towel over it. Lastly I brushed w/ an egg wash before popping them into the oven to give them a beautiful color. They came out soft, fluffy, and beautiful! 

Highly, highly recommend this recipe!

I've been making a smaller batch version of this recipe for Years. I use my bread machine to do the work and when its all done rising for the second time I take them out - shape them on a cookie sheet and let them rise again. In fact the recipe came from my grandma. We all call them buns LOL because that is what they called them back then. It is a must have for the holidays and they taste amazing. My mom used to make XL batch and freeze them. They still tasted as if they were just made.

I use a bread machine to make the dough, reducing the milk to 1.5 to 2 c and the flour to 5 to 6 c depending on how much I'm making then bake in the oven and it turns out wonderfully. I love this recipe, it is the best dinner roll recipe one I've found and always turns out well.
Angie, these awesome rolls are the bomb! I made my dough in a bread machine and added 2 TB of gluten flour for a nice rise. Perfection and OMG good!

I found this recipe to be great. I believe after the first mix the the dough needs to be kneaded to get the dough correct and started. In looking over the bad reviews , going to a no knead dough is incorrect for this recipe. I kneaded the dough on the first mix and then followed the recipe after that and got a perfect dinner roll.

Amazing! I used this recipe for bierocks dough and they couldn't have turned out any better. I ran short on all-purpose flour and had to use 2 cups of whole wheat to finish the recipe, other than that, no changes. I only let rise once, made the bierocks, then one more rise and popped them in the oven. Perfection. Thanks so much for this recipe!

I followed the ingredient list and it made enough rolls for three pans not one. I like that there's no kneading needed. But the texture was a little crumbly and had less of the elasticity I usually associate with yeast rolls and that is probably why. I added garlic and herbs to the melted butter before brushing the tops and they tasted amazing.
Really good recipe and easy to make...a little TLC and you get wonderful rolls.
Great recipe. Takes a while to go through all the rounds of rising , but well worth it.
This same recipe works in the bread machine. I had to bake it longer and covered, but they turned out great!
Takes a good bit of time and multiple proofings but these are the best rolls I've even eaten. The family LOVED them.
